description: Cool night, whole_house_fan home, outdoor air cooler than the 78 F bedroom: the window opens and natural ventilation starts (HVAC off, fan on). The cool offset is at its cap before the window opens; during and after ventilation the loop writes nothing.

events.note: The hallway thermostat's own sensor: satisfied, so it will not start by itself.
Seed the door/window sensor as closed.
Day classification (cold: heat all night / hot: cool all night).
Bedtime: the sleep band is written and the sleep window (remote sensor in use) begins.
The occupant opens the window; outdoor air is cooler: natural ventilation.
Bedroom warm; natural ventilation owns the house.
The hallway reading moves: the comfort check runs against the bedroom reading (78 F, above the sleep ceiling).

assertions.reason: Natural ventilation (the fan session) owns the house.
Precondition: the cool offset is at the -4 F cap before the window opens.
While ventilating (thermostat Off) and after the window closes, no loop write: the offset is never pushed into the ventilating house.

notes: Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md section 10), Issue #1194 increment (e). Tier A: the real ClimateAdvisorCoordinator + AutomationEngine under FakeHass/FakeScheduler (use_coordinator=true, so the sleep-sensor listener and the 1-minute timer are real); every assertion is track=integration for that reason and is evaluated, not skipped.

(a) Effectiveness: scratch-copy mutation run of this scenario against the production code (worktree untouched). It FAILS when M01: the whole offset deleted (the write path adds 0 and the check is a no-op); M02: the +4 F cap removed. Passes unmutated.

(b) Docs <-> production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md 'Remote-sensor outer loop on the thermostat setpoint (Issue #1194, increment a)': 'Gates' natural-ventilation row. Matches production. LIMIT: the thermostat is Off during ventilation, so the loop is inert there anyway (it never changes the mode); deleting the nat-vent term does not change this scenario's writes (M11). The gate term is proven in tests/test_remote_offset_gates_1194b.py.
(c) Occupant outcome if this regressed: The loop must not fight a ventilating house by pushing the AC setpoint.

verdict.summary: Natural ventilation owns the house; the loop stays out of it.
verdict.observed_behavior: result=natural_ventilation at 21:11; no set_temperature after the cap.
